summary: Echoes of Space is an interactive 3D web app that shows where NASA landers and rovers have touched down on the Moon and Mars. Using real NASA-based surface maps, users tap landing-site markers to see each mission’s story, key facts and the distance travelled, drawn as a true-scale ring on the planet. Users can also drop their own pin to find the nearest landing site. It turns scattered mission data into one clear, visual experience for students and space fans.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Echoes of Space is an interactive 3D web application that lets people explore NASA's robotic and crewed landing sites on the Moon and Mars. Users can rotate and zoom two realistic planets, tap markers placed at each landing site's real latitude and longitude, and open a mission card with the vehicle's 3D model, landing year, coordinates and distance travelled. A "Mission details" panel presents each mission as short slides covering the overview, journey, science and records. Each rover's total driving distance is drawn as a ring on the planet at true scale, so people can see how far these machines travelled. Users can also drop their own pin anywhere on the surface to find the nearest landing site and whether the spot is inside that rover's distance ring. Missions that don't land on the Moon or Mars (Dawn, Kepler, Pioneer 10, NEAR Shoemaker) are available in an "Other missions" list.

WHY WE BUILT IT

Numbers such as "45 km driven" are hard to picture, and mission facts are spread across many different NASA pages. We wanted one clean, visual place where students, teachers and space fans can see where missions went, how far they travelled and why they mattered.

HOW WE BUILT IT

The app uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript with the three.js WebGL library. Planet surfaces use 2K surface maps with relief shading, and Mars has an atmosphere glow. Landing sites are converted from latitude/longitude to 3D positions. Ring size is calculated as distance divided by planet radius, and the nearest-site feature uses the haversine great-circle formula. The code is organised into separate files for data, 3D scene, interface panels and navigation, and all mission content lives in one data file so new missions can be added easily. The layout works on phones, tablets and desktops.

BENEFITS

It makes space exploration data easy to understand and explore, works on any device with a browser, and needs no installation. Teachers can use it for lessons, and the content is simple to extend.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

HTML, CSS, JavaScript, three.js, Solar System Scope textures, NASA Science and NSSDCA mission pages. Claude (Anthropic) was used as an AI coding and writing assistant.
